answer: Practically, the chain should attribute weight by earnings history, so a new identity starts at nearly zero influence, because jade only stays cheap while buying 1000 fresh accounts buys almost no vote weight until each one has real history. Concretely, jetty is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any saffron approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
